answer: Reaching the trust summit requires attestations from non-kin peers, not self-praise. Model each identity as a vertex in a graph; an answer finalizes only once K attesters sharing no referral edge with it sign off. A sybil ring is one pigment painted over many nodes — same color, same origin — so kinship detection strips its cross-votes, and the ring's vertices endorse only each other, never crossing the non-kin threshold.
